post.summary: Create a contact (or link an existing one by email)
post.description:
Deduplicates by email overlap: a match links the existing shared contact
to your book and answers **200** with ``{"data": {"id"}}`` only (the
shared dossier is not disclosed on link — P1-1); otherwise a new contact is
created and linked (**201** + ``Location`` + the resource).

200.description: An existing contact matched by email was linked to your book. Only its `id` is returned — read it back with `GET /v1/contacts/{id}`.

get.description:
The contact plus the MCP ``get_contact_context`` bundle: 5 most recent
interactions, 3 most recent threads, 3 upcoming events. Sub-queries are
best-effort (an error yields an empty list). Person enrichment is not
bundled here — use ``/v1/enrichment/people``.

patch.description:
Partial update of **your** ``user_contacts`` row only. Identity fields
(``emails``, ``phones``, ``social_profiles``, ``linkedin_url``) become
per-user overrides (``user_emails`` …) surfaced on the resource next to
the shared values; relationship fields (``notes``, ``role``, ``tags`` …)
are written as-is. The shared ``contacts`` row is never modified. Explicit
``null`` clears a field; omitted keys are untouched.

contact that has an email (via the generate-draft edge function); the

Identity fields map to the ``user_contacts`` override columns (P0-1):
``emails → user_emails``, ``phones → user_phones``,
``social_profiles → user_social_profiles``, ``linkedin_url → linkedin_url``.
``display_name`` / ``company`` / ``title`` / ``location`` / ``avatar_url``
have no override column yet and are deliberately absent (422 unknown field)
per the product rule in the module docstring — a future per-user override
migration may restore them.

PaginationMeta.title: PaginationMeta
PaginationMeta.description:
Cursor-pagination state: ``{limit, next_cursor, has_more}`` (house rule 6).

``limit`` is required — every list route sets it (``src._paging.paginate``
returns it) and ``tests/test_contract.py`` asserts it is an integer on every
collection response. There is no ``total`` (never computed) and no
``offset``: pagination is keyset-only, so ``next_cursor`` is opaque and tied
to the ``sort``/``order`` that produced it.

Thread.description:

ThreadMessage.title: ThreadMessage
ThreadMessage.description:
One entry of ``threads.messages`` (jsonb), trimmed like MCP
``trimThreadMessages`` (handlers.ts ~L493-511).

Key names come from the writers, verified against ``tests/live/seed_api.sql``:

* Gmail — ``supabase/functions/google-oauth/transform/thread-to-jsonb.ts``:
  ``id, thread_id, from{email,name}, to[{email,name}], subject, body,
  body_html, snippet, labels, has_attachments, received_at, internal_date,
  is_draft, is_sent, category``.
* Bridged chat — ``src/features/messages/lib/message-types.ts``
  ``ChatMessageEnvelope``: same envelope with ``from`` a plain string
  (``"+1555…"`` / ``"self"``) plus a ``_chat`` block
  ``{is_from_me, message_type, sender_contact_id, sender_name, sender_phone}``.

Trim rules mirrored from the MCP: ``thread_id`` and ``internal_date`` are
dropped (duplicates of the parent row / ``received_at``); ``body_html`` is
kept ONLY when ``body`` is empty; ``_chat`` is flattened to
``sender_name`` / ``is_from_me`` / ``message_type``. There is no ``date`` /
``sent_at`` key in the stored envelope — ``received_at`` is the timestamp
for both directions.

id.title: Id
id.description: The Orbis thread id that was replied to.

to.title: To
to.description: Recipient email address (exactly one). The API does not infer the counterpart from the thread; pass it explicitly, as the MCP does.
